title: Quantitative Paper ELONA Protocol
author: Manuela De Las Casas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8hdht26

steps.title: Prepare Wax-Printed Nitrocellulose Strips
steps.instruction: Create wax-delimited dots on a nitrocellulose strip using a hot plate.

substeps.instruction: Set hot plate to 100ºC (or temperature sufficient to melt wax).
Melt a small amount of wax pencil on a Petri dish on the hot plate.
Cut a nitrocellulose sheet strip to the desired size.
Use the broad end of a 200μL pipette tip to pick up melted wax and press it onto the nitrocellulose strip to create circles.
Repeat to create all necessary dots for the assay.
Sandwich the strip between two sheets of paper and place on the hot plate with a Petri dish on top for pressure.
Warm for 5 minutes to allow wax penetration, then remove and let cool.
Verify that the center of the wax circles is clear.

steps.title: Prepare Aptamer Mix and Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a mixture of biotinylated and digoxigenin-tagged aptamers and create a serial dilution series.

substeps.instruction: Mix biotin-tagged Apta-Eco and digoxigenin-tagged reverse complementary Apta-Eco in an Eppendorf tube, ensuring both are at the same concentration (100 μM stock).
Add Aptamer Buffer (PBS, 1.4 mM Mg2+) in a 1:1:3 ratio (Aptamer A : Aptamer B : Buffer).
Perform serial dilutions to create 6 tubes with concentrations: 1, 1:2, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20, and 1:50.

steps.title: Heat-Treat and Conjugate Aptamers
steps.instruction: Heat the aptamer mix and conjugate it with streptavidin.

substeps.instruction: Heat the aptamer mix tube on a hot plate at 95ºC for 5 minutes.
Immediately transfer the tube to ice to cool.
Mix the cooled aptamer mix 1:1 with streptavidin (0.2 μg/μL or 18μM).
Incubate on ice for a few minutes to allow protein-aptamer bonding.

steps.title: Spot Samples and Controls
steps.instruction: Apply the aptamer-streptavidin mix and control solutions to the wax dots.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of the aptamer-streptavidin mix into the designated wax dots (2-3 dots per concentration) and allow to dry completely.
Prepare Negative Control 1: Pipette 5 μL of streptavidin (0.1 μg/mL) into reserved dots and allow to dry (no antibody added later).
Prepare Negative Control 2: Pipette 5 μL of streptavidin (0.1 μg/mL) into reserved dots and allow to dry (antibody added in later steps).
Prepare Positive Control 3: Pipette 5 μL of streptavidin (0.1 μg/mL) into reserved dots, allow to dry, then add 5 μL of antibody (Anti-Dig-POD 1:100 in PBS 1.4mM Mg2+ BSA 0.2%).

steps.title: Block the Membrane
steps.instruction: Block free spaces on the nitrocellulose membrane to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Place the strip in a Petri dish and pipette 5% BSA (in PBS).
Gently move the strip with tweezers and pipette away excess liquid.
Remove the strip and allow it to dry partially (not soaked, but not necessarily perfectly dry).

steps.title: Apply Antibody and Incubate
steps.instruction: Apply the detection antibody and incubate in a humid environment.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of antibody (Anti-Dig-POD 1:100 in PBS 1.4mM Mg2+ BSA 0.2%) onto the dots.
Incubate for one hour in a humid chamber (Petri dish with wet paper) to prevent complete drying.

steps.title: Wash and Dry Strips
steps.instruction: Wash the strips to remove unbound antibody and dry them.

substeps.instruction: Remove strips from the chamber and wash with PBS, using tweezers to move the strip and pipetting away excess liquid.
Allow the strip to dry partially.

steps.title: Develop Signal with ABTS
steps.instruction: Apply ABTS substrate to visualize the reaction.

substeps.instruction: Place strips in a humid chamber and pipette 10 μL of ABTS onto each dot.
Incubate for 30 minutes. (Optional: extend to 45 minutes if no color develops, or shorten to 15 minutes if color change is rapid).

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Analyze
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction simultaneously across all strips and analyze results.

substeps.instruction: Dry the strips on a hot plate at 95ºC for 5 minutes to stop the reaction.
Scan the strips for higher quality results.
Analyze the density of each dot using software tools.
